Commentary.Commentary: We are back for the chase! The umpires have made their way to the middle followed by the players of Zimbabwe. Pathum Nissanka and Kusal Mendis are the openers for the Lankans. While Richard Ngarava will bowl the first over.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

After winning the toss and putting Zimbabwe to bat, the Sri Lankans came out all guns blazing. Angelo Mathews made an impactful start by dismissing Craig Ervine for a golden duck in the opening over. Captain Wanindu Hasaranga led the bowling attack brilliantly, taking four crucial wickets. Maheesh Theekshana played a key role by delivering an excellent over in the powerplay and removing Tinashe Kamunhukamwe. Despite a challenging first over, Dilshan Madushanka made a strong comeback in his second over, bowling tighter lines and claiming the wicket of Zimbabwe's skipper Sikandar Raza. Sri Lanka's bowling performance has put them in a commanding position, and they will be optimistic about securing the series victory. Zimbabwe, however, will be deeply disappointed with their batting display. Following the early dismissal of Craig Ervine, Brian Bennett launched a counter-attack, scoring 18 runs off Dilshan Madushanka in the second over. Despite a decent start and a quick scoring rate in the powerplay, Zimbabwe lost their way afterward. Tinashe Kamunhukamwe got a promising start, but both he and Brian Bennett were dismissed cheaply. Apart from a brief innings by Sikandar Raza, no other batsman managed to make a significant impact. Zimbabwe will now need to outperform themselves and bowl their hearts out to restrict Sri Lanka. Can they pull out a rabbit from the hat and turn things around? Or will this chase be a walk in the park for Sri Lanka? Let's find out as the second innings comes to you shortly.

The first innings has come to a close, and what a spectacle it has been. Sri Lanka have put up a show and are in the driver's seat knocking off Zimbabwe for just 82 runs in 14.1 overs. Zimbabwe have had a collapse in this crucial decider match losing the last 6 wickets for just 11 runs.

As a result, he gets the elevation but not the distance as the ball goes miles up in the air towards long on, Dasun Shanaka runs forward, settles under it and takes a good catch. Zimbabwe have been bowled out for 82!

OUT! BLINDER AT POINT! What a catch! What a start for Sri Lanka as well! Angelo Mathews serves this full again, on middle, nips away a bit, Craig Ervine looks to flick it away, but closes the face of the bat early and gets a leading edge as the ball flies wide of point. Sadeera Samarawickrama there flies to his right to take a stunning one-handed catch and uses his other hand to hold on to it in the end. Early blow for Zimbabwe as Ervine goes back for a golden duck!

Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the decider in Colombo! The players are already out in the middle now. Tinashe Kamunhukamwe and Craig Ervine are the two openers for Zimbabwe. Angelo Mathews has the new ball in hand and is raring to go. Let's play...

Sikandar Raza, the captain of Zimbabwe says the win was a long time coming for them. He continues saying the ODI matches they played against them were really close and to come on top was really pleasing. They wanted to bat first as it looks dry and it will spin. Only one change Tony Munyonga comes in for Ryan Burl.

Wanindu Hasaranga, the skipper of Sri Lanka says the dew is the main concern because of which he decided to chase. He then talks about the only issue with batting which needs to click and the top 4 will need to perform better, especially in the middle overs. He then concludes the two changes in the playing XI with Dhananjaya De Silva and Kamindu Mendis coming in for Charith Asalanka and Kusal Janith Perera.

Farveez Maharoof says the pitch is the same one that was used the last time. 70 meters all round from the pitch. But the pitch is too hard and not a lot of crack on it. Farveez thinks the team who will win the toss would like to chase today as dew would be a huge factor and the humidity is high in Colombo.

Zimbabwe (Playing XI) - Tinashe Kamunhukamwe, Craig Ervine, Brian Bennett, Sikandar Raza (C), Sean Williams, Tony Munyonga (In place of Ryan Burl), Luke Jongwe, Clive Madande (WK), Wellington Masakadza, Blessing Muzarabani, Richard Ngarava.

Sri Lanka (Playing XI) - Pathum Nissanka, Kusal Mendis (WK), Sadeera Samarawickrama, Kamindu Mendis (In place of Charith Asalanka​​​​​), Angelo Mathews, Dhananjaya de Silva (In place of Kusal Perera), Dasun Shanaka, Wanindu Hasaranga (C), Maheesh Theekshana, Dushmantha Chameera, Dilshan Madushanka.
TOSS - The coin lands in favour of Sri Lanka and they have elected to BOWL first.

On the other hand, it was a match to forget for Sri Lanka and all they can do is to focus on this game. Lankan's top order totally collapsed in the initial stage of the innings but vice-captain, Charith Asalanka and the veteran, Angelo Mathews anchored the situation with all their experience and cooked a strong and firm partnership of 118 off just 79 deliveries. Although, their bowlers managed to pick up wickets at regular intervals, but just like their opponents, they were a bit too expensive at the death which cost them the game. They just need to correct and check a few pointers, but other than that it was pretty decent from them. Can Sri Lanka mount a comeback to secure the series, or will Zimbabwe complete an inspiring turnaround for a series win? We will find out soon. Toss and team news in a bit.

Zimbabwe made history in the previous match by winning for the first time in this format against the Lankans. Special credit to Luke Jongwe and Clive Madande only who stole the match from the opposition's pocket in the death overs. Craig Ervine also played a brilliant knock of crucial 70 runs which provided the platform. Their bowling unit also did well putting the hosts in a critical situation by picking up four wickets in the Powerplay, but failed to build on that and allowed the opposition to stretch the target further. The Chevrons would like to continue with the same aggressiveness and create more history by getting a famous series win.

Hello and a warm welcome folks! It is time for some more exciting cricket action as we build up to the final game of this three-match T20 series where Sri Lanka takes on Zimbabwe at R.Premadasa Stadium. The excitement is palpable as the battle between these two sides turns into a curveball as this is the decider. The forecast says that there will be clouds around, but we hope that this series gets decided on the field.
... MATCHDAY ...

The third and decisive T20I match between Sri Lanka and Zimbabwe is upon us, with the series deadlocked at 1-1 following Zimbabwe's jaw-dropping triumph in the previous game. The clash went down to the wire, and it was Luke Jongwe who emerged as the undisputed hero with his valuable cameo of 25 runs off 12 balls, orchestrating a sensational finish by chasing 20 off the last over that sent shockwaves through the Sri Lankan camp. Now, the third T20I is the decider and it’s the R. Premadasa Stadium that will host this match yet again. With Charith Asalanka and the Sri Lankan veteran Angelo Mathews stepping up in the last game and getting into the grooves, their batting line-up with Kusal Mendis does look dangerous. Though the Sri Lankan skipper Wanindu Hasaranga was expensive in the previous encounter, the bowling line-up of Sri Lanka including Maheesh Theekshana, Dushmantha Chameera, and Dilshan Madushanka, has all the requisite ingredients to pull things back in their favor. Craig Ervine has looked consistent for the visitors along with Joylord Gumbie. the others need to step up and contribute with the bat. Sikandar Raza has been quiet with the bat and ball and he will aim to perform better. Ervine’s brilliant 70 and fireworks from Luke Jongwe at the backend of the run-chase helped Zimbabwe cross the victory line. The latter contributed with the ball as well by picking two crucial wickets. Blessing Muzarabani and Richard Ngarava will be expected to bowl well and provide timely breakthroughs for their team. It is Zimbabwe's last T20I match before the T20 World Cup, 2024, and they will surely aim to finish up on a positive note with a series win. As for the hosts Sri Lanka, they still have the Afghanistan series coming up but their priority would be to take the series and prevent a setback. Sri Lanka definitely has an upper hand in head-to-head, but they won't consider Zimbabwe as an easy escape, especially after the result of the second match. So cricket enthusiasts, who will take the series?
